content.text:
`del(.[nan])` and `del(.[nan, nan])` now return the array unchanged and finish immediately. I checked this against the built `jq` binary.

I made two changes in `src/jv_aux.c`:
- **`jv_dels`:** a NaN index on an array is now skipped, since it isn't a valid index. Before, it matched neither the negative nor the non-negative check and fell through to the wrong path.
- **`delpaths_sorted`:** the grouping index `j` now starts at `i + 1`. Because `jv_equal(nan, nan)` is false, `j` used to never advance past `i`, which was the infinite loop.

I also added two tests to `tests/jq.test` covering both cases. Other deletions mixed with NaN still work: `[1,2,3] | del(.[nan,0])` gives `[2,3]`.

In `jq --run-tests tests/jq.test`, 519 of 531 tests pass. The same suite on the unmodified code gave 517 of 529, so my two new tests pass and the other 12 failed before my change. I didn't look into why those 12 fail. The 9 malformed ones are mostly "module not found" errors.
